files.text:
Light through stone lace

A jali is a window cut from a single slab, and the cutting is the whole design. The sun does the rest: it falls through the stars and polygons, and the floor becomes a second, brighter screen.

Walk along the wall and the day goes with you. Each window throws its lace at the angle of its own hour, sharp as the stone near the sill, melting into warm glow across the room.

# jali-light A row of real stone windows and the sun that crosses them. Four photographed jalis (Sidi Saiyyed's tree of life, two from Humayun's Tomb, a floral screen from Kusru Bagh) hang in a dark stone wall; a flagstone floor runs toward you. Scroll and you walk along the wall while the sun climbs: a cold grey dawn at the first window, gold, white noon, amber evening at the last, each window throwing its lace across the stones at the angle of its own hour. Everything you see is a photograph (windows, wall, floor); the only thing made in code is the light. Colour is earned: the room is grey until the sun warms it. ## Markup ```html ``` Or `import { jaliLight } from './jali-light.js'; const destroy = jaliLight(figure, { start: 1 });` Each `` is one window: a photograph (soft alpha edges so its dark surround melts into the wall) with a twin beside it named `-mask.webp` (or set `data-mask`): the same view in greyscale, white where daylight comes through and black on stone. Make the mask by thresholding the photograph's own luminance: a window shot from inside against bright daylight gives an exact one (that is how these four were made). `data-h` is the window's height in the room's units (about metres); its width follows from the photograph. The script wraps the figure in a `.jl-track` (the tall scroll lane the figure sticks in) unless you made one yourself. Without script the windows sit in a row you can scroll along. ## Atmosphere (`air.js`) - **Shafts:** each window's own lace is swept through the air along the sun's direction in forty thin slices, softer and fainter farther out, every slice cut off at the floor, so a shaft ends exactly where its patch of light begins. A slow mist thickens and thins it, and a faint haze lifts the far end of the room. Brightness and colour follow the hour as you walk. - **Dust:** three depths of motes (far and tiny, mid, and a few near ones out of focus), drawn only as bright as the beam they sit in, so they blink on and off as they cross the lace. Warm air lifts them in the beam, a faint draught pushes them along, and a mote that has drifted into shade respawns in the light. Depth parallax shifts them with the pointer and tilt; they never react to a pointer or a finger. - **Glints:** a slow highlight on the rim of each glass orb, grains of mica in the lit floor, and a twinkle on the stone edge of a window. - Cost: shafts draw on a 0.4x canvas at 30 a second, dust and glints on one canvas; both stop when the piece is off screen. ## Options | `data-` attribute | option | default | | |---|---|---|---| | `data-screens` | `screens` | the `` srcs | comma-separated image URLs, if you do not want `` children | | `data-mask` (on each ``) | `masks` | `-mask.webp` | the greyscale lattice mask for that window | | `data-h` (on each ``) | `heights` | `1.9` | window height in room units | | `data-wall` | `wall` | `wall.webp` beside the first screen | seamless wall tile (a scanned stone texture or any stone photograph) | | `data-floor` | `floor` | `floor.webp` beside the first screen | seamless floor tile | | `data-start` | `start` | `1` | the window shown in the reduced-motion still, counting from 0 | | `data-intensity` | `intensity` | `.7` | 0 to 1: how strong the shafts, dust and glints are | | `data-motes` | `motes` | `700` | specks of dust in the room (half that on a phone); `0` for none | | `data-dust="off"` | `dust: false` | on | no dust | | `data-shafts="off"` | `shafts: false` | on | no shafts of light or haze | | `data-glimmer="off"` | `glimmer: false` | on | no glints on the orbs, floor or window stone | Theming: the figure fills the viewport height (`height`, `min-height` in the CSS); `--jl-n` on the track is set for you. The scroll length is `70svh` per window (the last rule in `jali-light.css`). The day's palette (sun, sky, ambient, gain, colour amount) is the `STOPS` table at the top of `jali-light.js`; the room's size is the constants above it. ## Orbs: things in the room In front of each window hangs one **orb** (`orbs.js`, imported by `jali-light.js`): a ball of frosted glass with a thin-line glyph in it, hung in the room's own geometry between the window and you. It travels with the walk and moves more than the wall behind it; the pointer or the phone's tilt turns it a little toward you; it bobs slowly. The sun's lace falls across the glass (the same beam lookup that lights the floor is read over its face), the rim light takes the hour's colour, and on the floor beneath it sit a soft shadow and a small bright pool of focused light. A **gaze reticle** follows the mouse; over an orb its ring opens and fills (on a phone the ring blooms where you tap). Click, tap or Enter and the orb unfolds into a floating glass window, a small app. Escape, the close button or a tap outside folds it back and returns focus to the orb. Four apps ship, one per window: **profile** (a card with an avatar, a name and three link rows; "Your Name" is placeholder text), **code** (an editor with a tiny highlighted snippet, two file tabs, a blinking caret), **social** (a feed of three posts; the heart toggles and counts) and **gallery** (the windows' own photographs, with arrows and thumbnails). Everything is placeholder content to be replaced. Configure on each ``: ```html ``` | `data-` attribute | option (`orbs[i]`) | default | | |---|---|---|---| | `data-orb` | `label` | by window: About me, Code, Social, Photographs | the orb's accessible name, and the word that appears when you look at it | | `data-glyph` | `glyph` | `user`, `code`, `chat`, `photo` | a name from `GLYPHS` in `orbs.js` (`user code chat photo note mail`), or an SVG fragment on a 24-unit grid | | `data-app` | `app` | `profile`, `code`, `social`, `gallery` | which app opens | | `data-orbs="off"` on the figure | `orbs: false` | on | no orbs at all | Options object: `jaliLight(figure, { orbs: [{ label, glyph, app }, ...], apps: { name: (host) => HTMLElement | { el, destroy } }, glyphs: { name: '' } })`. An app builder receives `{ images(), index, label }` and returns the element that goes inside the glass window. `jali:open` (detail `{ app, label }`) and `jali:close` fire on the figure. Where each orb hangs (height, depth, drift off the window's centre) is the `SPOTS` table in `orbs.js`; the look is the `.jl-orb` rules in the CSS (`--jl-sun`, `--jl-sky` are set on the figure from the hour).
